# Genesis Apocryphon Column 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 20 | **Condition:** Well preserved; the famous beauty hymn is substantially intact

---

**20:1** Sarai wept that night because of what I had said. We traveled on and arrived at Zoan,

**20:2** and Sarai urged me again regarding all the land of Egypt: Tell them he is my brother,

**20:3** so that I may live because of you. And Sarai wept again that night.

**20:4** Then Harkenosh arrived [...] with Lot, and Lot told him [...] about Abram's wife [...]

**20:5** Harkenosh brought lavish gifts of silver, gold, and fine linen [...] to the king.

**20:6** How beautiful is her face, how fine the hair of her head!

**20:7** How lovely her eyes, how pleasing the curve of her nose

**20:8** and all the radiance of her face! How beautiful her breasts,

**20:9** how perfect her luminous skin! Her arms — how beautiful!

**20:10** Her hands — how graceful! How lovely the palms of her hands!

**20:11** How long and elegant her fingers! Her feet — how beautiful!

**20:12** Her thighs — how smooth! No virgin or bride entering the wedding chamber

**20:13** is lovelier than she. Her beauty surpasses every woman;

**20:14** she outshines them all. And alongside all this beauty

**20:15** she possesses great wisdom, and everything about her is beautiful.

**20:16** When the king heard Harkenosh's report, along with that of his two companions

**20:17** — for all three spoke with one voice — his desire for her was overwhelming.

**20:18** He sent for her at once, and when he saw her he was stunned by her beauty.

**20:19** He claimed her as his wife and tried to have me killed.

**20:20** But Sarai told the king: He is my brother. So I, Abram, was spared because of her.

**20:21** That night I wept bitterly — I, Abram, and my nephew Lot with me —

**20:22** because Sarai had been torn from me by force.

**20:23** I spent the night in prayer, pleading and begging for mercy,

**20:24** tears streaming down my face, and I cried out:

**20:25** Blessed are You, God Most High, Lord of all the ages!

**20:26** You are Lord and Master of all! You rule over every king on earth,

**20:27** bringing judgment on them all. Now I bring my case before You, my Lord,

**20:28** against Pharaoh Zoan, king of Egypt — my wife has been seized from me by force!

**20:29** Bring judgment on him for my sake! Let me see Your mighty hand

**20:30** strike him down, him and his entire household!

**20:31** Do not let him defile my wife this very night!

**20:32** Let them all know that You are Lord over every king on earth!

**20:33** Then I wept, and fell silent.

**20:34** That very night, God Most High sent a plague-spirit against him,

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 20 is well preserved. The beauty hymn (20:6-15) is one of the great literary achievements of Second Temple literature — an extended blazon that catalogs Sarai's beauty from face to feet. The dynamic rendering streamlines the anaphoric repetition while preserving its cumulative force. "Luminous skin" (20:9) captures the Aramaic term for radiant whiteness. The prayer escalates in emotional intensity toward the column's climax. "Plague-spirit" (20:34) renders the Aramaic rucha mare'ita in accessible English.*
